subhero.p_2: A sample of how a week unfolds. Every journey is shaped to your group, your pace, and the calendar. This is only a starting point.
subhero.p_3: Settle into Willemstad and enjoy a welcome dinner overlooking the historic harbor. An opening conversation introduces the program and themes of the coming days.
subhero.p_4: Walk across the floating Queen Emma Bridge into historic Punda. A specialist historian traces how Sephardic settlers transformed a small Dutch outpost into an influential Atlantic port. At a visit to one of the oldest Jewish cemeteries in the Western Hemisphere, carved stones reveal Iberian roots and far-reaching family ties. The afternoon concludes with a candid discussion on slavery, emancipation, and the intertwined histories of Jewish and Afro-Curaçaoan life.
subhero.p_5: Experience the oldest synagogue in continuous use in the Americas, where a sand-covered floor and Sephardic rituals preserve nearly three centuries of congregational life. Explore ceremonial objects and family histories at the newly expanded Jewish Museum Curaçao. Later, venture through the mansions of Scharloo, while learning from current owners about the neighborhood’s lively past, as well as the profound role of the Afro-Curaçaoan caregivers who transmitted language and culture across generations, and in Jewish homes. When the calendar permits, guests join the local community for Shabbat services and an intimate dinner with the local Chabad rabbi, his family, and members of the community.
subhero.text_alt_1: Cazinha dos Cohanim, Beth Haim Bleinheim Cementery
subhero.p_6: People-to-people encounters: conversations with community members, and a kosher lunch in the Sephardic tradition.
subhero.p_7: A gentler day: the coastline, the markets, and time to rest before Shabbat.
subhero.p_8: Kabbalat Shabbat with the congregation, and a hosted Shabbat dinner as the light fades over the harbour.
subhero.p_9: A slow morning and private transfer to the airport, leaving as family, not as visitors.
